neet_phy_u07_t08_1.working: A soap bubble has two surfaces, so ΔP = 4S/R = 4(0.03)/0.02 = 6 Pa.

neet_phy_u07_t08_2.working: An air bubble in water has one surface. P = P0 + ρgh + 2S/r = 1e5 + 1000 + 1400 = 1.024e5 Pa.

neet_phy_u07_t08_3.working: Interface radius r = r1·r2/(r2 − r1) = 24/2 = 12 cm.

neet_phy_u07_t08_4.working: Excess pressure 4S/R is larger in the smaller bubble, so air flows from small to large and A is true. R is false because ΔP is inversely proportional to R.

neet_phy_u07_t08_5.working: In vacuum, isothermal: ΣPV is conserved, so Σr² is conserved, giving r = √(9+16) = 5 cm, not 7 cm. Statement I is false. A cylindrical surface gives ΔP = S/R, half of 2S/R for a drop, so Statement II is true.
